**Fixed session-end-ship test that shipped the lane for real under npm test (#1011, #1012)**

**What**: Replaced the 'real entrypoint run (flag false)' test in brain/scripts/memory/session-end-ship.test.mjs with a flag-agnostic version: it reads the real tracked config through loadBrainConfig(), derives the expected spawn count from memory.lane.enabled, drives shipOnSessionEnd through the module's _spawn/_tmpdir seams, and checks the real OS tmpdir by before/after snapshot instead of asserting absence.
**Why**: The old test spawned the unmocked entrypoint against the real repo with the real credential in process.env. Its safety was the flag being false. When #890 flipped memory.lane.enabled to true, npm test pushed a memory lane branch, opened PR #1007 and auto-merged it into main with no human involved. The same test also failed on any machine that had shipped a lane that day (#1011).
**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/session-end-ship.test.mjs (one file, +67/-22, commit 2133ebc3 on fix/issue-1011-fixtest-session-end-ships-flag-false-tes).
**Learned**: A test whose safety depends on a configuration value is safe by coincidence. The repo already had the BRAIN_VCS_TEST_MODULE seam for CLI-level ship tests; this file sat outside it. #1012 owns the class: a structural invoker guard in the runtime, a sweep of every test that spawns a real entrypoint, and an anti-pattern draft for human promotion.
